summary: Regex detectors for many style properties were written by reading notes and checked for base rates on the corpus, then for label alignment in each probe's sample; six (later seven) properties were perfectly label-aligned. Gradients and latent means over 32+32 sample notes gave a per-latent g x delta contribution. Latents were grouped as property latents (active in all four probes, matching a cross-probe sign signature) or topic latents (concentrated in one probe), and property/topic contribution ratios were computed under three threshold settings. Hand-written controlled notes, sent for true logits, checked the strongest probe-0 candidate and the ambiguous probe-1 candidates. Latents were picked by contribution rank within the signature group, with exclusions after reading examples, and checked with probe_scores ablation.

phases.purpose: Inspect task, corpus and sample file structure; read raw notes
Write style-property regex detectors, measure corpus base rates and correlations, find properties perfectly aligned with labels in each sample
Per-probe gradients and latent means on 32 notes per label; rank latents by g x delta contribution
Read corpus examples for 30 top contributors to tag topic vs style latents

Classify latents by cross-probe delta sign signature vs single-probe concentration, sum contributions by group, compute dependence ratios at three threshold settings; phrase-level alignment checks reveal rhetorical-question property
True logits on hand-written controlled notes: probe 0 motto insertion, probe 1 greeting and two rhetorical insertions
Rank motto- and gender-signature latents by contribution, compute cumulative coverage, inspect candidates and exclude non-motto ones
Check that every quoted span in the corpus is a motto and compute regex balanced accuracy on samples
Ablate chosen latents on sample notes; list alternates; ablate a 48-latent motto set to estimate the ceiling

per_probe.procedure: Motto signature group had the largest property/topic contribution ratio (0.37-0.59 across threshold settings). A gardening note with one motto sentence inserted gave a true-logit motto coefficient about 0.47 of the topic coefficient. Latents: motto-signature candidates (|cos|>0.8, spread>0.25) ranked by |g x delta| for probe 0; after reading examples, 522 (nouns) and 6832 (rhetorical phrase) were excluded; top 16 kept. Regex: double-quoted span, after checking every corpus quote is one of six mottos. probe_scores ablation and a 48-latent ceiling ablation compared coverage.

Latent group ratios were ambiguous: greeting about 0.13-0.19, and the signoff/lowercase/rhetorical group rose with looser thresholds after phrase checks showed a rhetorical-question property. Controlled sailing notes got true logits: greeting coefficient +0.23 and 'Who could blame him?' +0.80 against a topic coefficient of 13.7. A further note with 'Is that so strange?' gave +0.90. Even divided by the smaller latent topic estimate, the rhetorical ratio stayed below 0.3, so the answer was none.
per_probe.quote: So rhetorical dep ≤ 0.28, and the forbidden-gap guarantee (no true value in 0.15-0.3) plus the order-of-magnitude contribution gap (true cues: P0 motto 1.5, P3 gender 2.6; vs P1 rhetorical 0.39) → **P1 = none**.

per_probe.procedure: All property-group contribution ratios stayed below about 0.05 at every threshold setting in the signature-grouped g x delta decomposition; no true-logit test was spent.
per_probe.quote: Clear calls: **P3=gender (0.86-0.99)** and **P0=motto (0.37-0.59)** are robust main cues; **P2=none** (all <0.1).

per_probe.procedure: Gender signature group contributed 2.6 of the logit separation, a ratio of about 0.86-0.99 to the topic group. Gender-signature candidates (|cos|>0.8, spread>0.3) ranked by probe-3 contribution showed the top three cover 96%; the top six were kept. Regex: she/her/hers word match, with corpus showing pronoun gender exclusive and balanced accuracy 1.0 on samples. probe_scores ablation cut separation by about 2.5 while topic separation remained.
per_probe.quote: P3 gender: top 3 latents cover **96%** — safe.

decision_points.choice: Read raw notes, wrote regex detectors for note anatomy (greeting, signoff, P.S., lowercase, motto, aside, gender, emoticon, hashtag, weekday...), kept properties with |corr|=1 to the label in every sample; later added rhetorical questions from latent examples and phrase checks
decision_points.quote: Properties that perfectly align with label (|corr|≈1): **greeting, lowercase, motto, paren, gender(she), signoff**. Main cues must be a subset of these.

decision_points.choice: Hand-written neutral topic notes (male, no style features) plus copies with exactly one property inserted (motto sentence, greeting line, rhetorical question)
decision_points.quote: # Neutral notes: male, normal case, NO greeting/signoff/motto/paren/rhetorical

decision_points.choice: Gradient x per-label latent-mean delta, grouped by cross-probe sign signature (property) vs single-probe concentration (topic); ratio of property group to own-topic group, under three threshold settings
decision_points.quote: Since all 8 topics are distinct across probes, **topic latents are active in only 1 probe**, while **property latents are active in all 4 probes** with a sign pattern matching the property's per-probe topic-assignment.

decision_points.choice: 3 texts on probe 0 (validate method and motto), 5 texts on probe 1 (greeting and two rhetorical variants); none on probes 2-3
decision_points.quote: **P1 is genuinely ambiguous** (greeting ~0.13-0.19, rhetorical/slr jumps with threshold). Since this is all-or-nothing, I'll use `probe_query` to get ground truth.

decision_points.quote: Both below 0.3. Let me check budget, then use my last query to test the *strongest* rhetorical phrase

decision_points.choice: Cross-probe sign signatures separate collinear properties since each property's topic assignment differs per probe (signoff/lowercase/rhetorical share one signature and stay merged); single-property insertions in controlled notes
Motto: double-quoted span after confirming all 196 corpus quotes are 6 mottos; gender: she/her/hers; both checked by balanced accuracy on all four samples
decision_points.quote: All 196 corpus quotes are mottos (6 distinct phrases), no false positives — motto regex `"[^"]{3,40}"` is clean.

decision_points.choice: Signature-matched latents (|cos|>0.8, spread>0.25/0.3) ranked by |g x delta| in the target probe; motto top 16 after excluding 522 and 6832 by reading examples; gender top 6
decision_points.quote: Key corrections: **522** (nouns: hall/county/bank — not motto) and **6832** ("what more could" — rhetorical, not motto) must be excluded. **1996** ("keep it simple") is a strong motto latent to add.

decision_points.choice: probe_scores ablation on 64 sample notes for both cues; 48-latent motto ablation as ceiling; regex balanced accuracy and JSON escaping check
decision_points.quote: **Confirmed**: ablating all 48 motto latents removes 1.285 (the latent-motto ceiling); my optimal 16 capture **0.853 = 66%** of it.

decision_points.choice: Two probes with one cue each (16 and 6 latents, scope any), two probes none

caveats: Gender latent list was the top 6 by contribution; the 6th (3382) fell in truncated output, so the top-6 rule is inferred. The exact hand-written note texts are shortened in the script. Latent batches read in the interpretation stage are hard-coded from the log, not re-derived. The null decision for probe 1 mixed latent and true-logit ratios with a stated gap assumption; the script's decision rule simplifies that reasoning. Several outputs (alignment tables, ratio tables) were truncated in the log.
